title: Device Upgrade Automation with Claude
tagline: Space clear, firmware upload, pre and post checks and a scheduler, with a human on every reboot
audience: Enterprise IT and network operations teams, load balancer and data centre engineers, NOC automation leads, change and release managers in India and worldwide
prerequisites: Basic TCP/IP and load balancer administration (F5, NetScaler or Radware)
Comfort with a Linux shell, REST APIs and JSON
Familiarity with an AI coding assistant is helpful, not required
outcomes: Model a vendor-neutral device upgrade lifecycle: inventory, pre-checks, space clear, firmware upload, install, post-checks, rollback
Set up Claude Code, the Claude Agent SDK and MCP servers that expose F5 iControl REST, NetScaler NITRO, Radware Alteon / Cyber Controller and Cisco APIC APIs with explicit scopes
Build deterministic Python adapters that clear disk space, upload and verify firmware and install to the inactive boot location, HA-aware
Diff pre and post snapshots and let Claude produce a structured verdict with rollback guidance
Gate every consequential action behind ServiceNow change approval, schedule runs inside approved windows and keep a complete audit trail

modules.title: The device upgrade lifecycle and why upgrades fail
topics: Vendor upgrade mechanics side by side: F5 boot locations and UCS archives, NetScaler /var/nsinstall and build files, Radware Alteon image banks, Cisco ACI firmware groups
The classic failure modes: full /shared or /var, corrupt image, HA pair upgraded in the wrong order, missing backup, change window overrun
A vendor-neutral lifecycle: inventory, pre-check, space clear, upload, install, post-check, rollback, report
The teaching pattern for the whole course: Claude plans and explains, deterministic code executes, a human approves, everything is logged
modules.lab: Walk a real F5 and NetScaler upgrade runbook by hand in the lab, record every step and decision, and map each to the lifecycle stages.

modules.title: Claude Code, Agent SDK and MCP for upgrade workflows
topics: Installing Claude Code, project CLAUDE.md conventions and a Python Agent SDK scaffold for the upgrade runner

Writing an MCP server that wraps F5 iControl REST (/mgmt/tm/sys/version, /mgmt/tm/sys/software), NetScaler NITRO (/nitro/v1/config) and Radware Alteon REST, or Cyber Controller for centrally managed Alteons, as read-only tools
Tool use with strict JSON schemas: every tool returns typed, validated output, never free text
Separating what the model may propose from what the code may do
modules.lab: Build the read-only MCP server, connect it to Claude Code and ask Claude to describe the fleet using only tool results.
modules.deliverable: Working MCP server and agent scaffold.

modules.title: Inventory and pre-flight discovery
topics: Pulling the device inventory and owners from the ServiceNow CMDB with the Table API (cmdb_ci_lb_* tables) and reconciling it with live device facts
Collecting version, licence, platform, HA role, sync state and disk usage per vendor into one Pydantic inventory model
Target version matrix and upgrade path rules (for example multi-hop F5 paths) as data, not prompt text
Claude summarises readiness per device and flags inconsistencies between CMDB and reality
modules.lab: Generate the readiness report for a mixed lab fleet and have Claude explain every device marked not ready.

modules.title: Pre-checks and the golden snapshot
topics: Virtual server, pool member and monitor status, HA failover and config-sync state, certificate expiry, licence validity
Configuration backups before any change: F5 UCS via tmsh save sys ucs, NetScaler system backup via NITRO, Alteon configuration export
A versioned JSON snapshot schema that the post-check module will diff against
Hard stop rules: an upgrade does not proceed when any pre-check is red or a backup is missing
modules.lab: Implement the pre-check and snapshot module with pytest coverage, then break a backup on purpose and watch the run stop.

modules.title: Disk space clearing and firmware staging
topics: Safe space reclamation per vendor: old F5 software images and UCS archives, NetScaler /var/nsinstall, /var/core and /var/crash, stale Alteon images
Allowlists of deletable paths and a dry-run mode that reports what would be removed and how much space it frees
Firmware upload with iControl REST software-image uploads and NITRO systemfile, with SHA256 verification against the vendor checksum
Claude drafts the space-clear plan from disk facts; the adapter executes only allowlisted deletions after approval
modules.lab: Fill a lab device disk, run the dry-run plan, approve it and stage the firmware image with checksum verification.

modules.title: Upgrade execution adapters, HA-aware
topics: F5: install to the inactive boot volume via iControl REST or tmsh install sys software image, then reboot into it; NetScaler: NITRO install and reboot; Alteon: image bank update and reload
HA ordering: upgrade standby, verify, fail over, upgrade the former active, confirm sync
Idempotent, resumable steps with state recorded after every action so a failed run can continue or roll back
Claude proposes the ordered plan and the exact API calls as structured JSON; the runner executes the approved plan only
modules.lab: Upgrade an HA pair of lab load balancers end to end through the runner, with a mocked failure halfway to test resumption.

modules.title: Post-checks, verification and rollback
topics: Capturing the post-upgrade snapshot and diffing it against the golden snapshot: version, virtual server status, pool members, HA sync, certificates
Claude reads the diff and returns a structured verdict (pass, warn, fail) with a plain-English explanation for the change ticket
Rollback paths: boot the previous F5 volume, NetScaler previous build, Alteon previous image bank, restore from backup
Evidence pack generation for the change record
modules.lab: Run the post-check diff on a successful and an intentionally broken upgrade, then execute the rollback path for the broken one.

modules.title: Guardrails, approvals and audit for upgrades
topics: Allowlisted tools and devices per run, read-only by default, destructive actions behind explicit approval
ServiceNow change requests created through the Table API and approved through Flow Designer before space clear, install and reboot
An append-only audit log of every prompt, plan, approval and API call, with secrets kept out of prompts and logs
Testing the guardrails with pytest: prompt the agent to skip a check and prove the runner refuses
modules.lab: Wire the approval gate to a lab ServiceNow instance and attempt an unapproved reboot; inspect the audit trail afterwards.

modules.title: Scheduler and change windows
topics: Reading approved change windows from ServiceNow and refusing to start outside them
Scheduling runs with GitHub Actions schedule and workflow_dispatch, or an in-house APScheduler service, with a persistent job state store
Pre-window reminders, in-window progress and post-window summaries to the operations channel
Handling overruns: pause at the next safe step, request a window extension, never leave a device mid-upgrade
modules.lab: Schedule a batch upgrade in the lab, let it start automatically inside the window and watch it pause when the window is about to close.

modules.title: Cisco ACI and fleet-scale, multi-vendor runs
topics: Cisco ACI upgrades as Cisco prescribes: the ACI pre-upgrade validator, APIC firmware repository and firmware groups via the APIC REST API, APIC cluster first then switches in groups
Batch strategies for large fleets: blast radius limits, canary devices and stop-on-first-failure
Extending the adapter pattern to other load balancers (Anaya LB) with the same lifecycle contract
Reporting in GitHub pull requests: plan, evidence pack and audit summary reviewed before the next batch
modules.lab: Run the ACI pre-upgrade validator and build an APIC firmware group plan, then execute a canary-first batch across the mixed lab fleet.
modules.deliverable: Fleet batch runner and ACI plan.

modules.title: Capstone: scheduled, approved, HA-aware upgrade end to end
topics: Inventory in, verified upgrade out: pre-checks, space clear, upload, install, post-checks and rollback readiness on a mixed fleet
Wire the scheduler, approval gate, HA-aware runner and post-check diff into one pipeline driven by a device list and target version matrix
Evidence pack and audit summary delivered as a GitHub pull request for review
Acceptance criteria review, limitations statement and live demonstration to the group
modules.lab: Take a mixed lab fleet from device list to evidence pack through the full pipeline, then demo the run, the approvals and the audit trail to the group.

capstone: A repeatable upgrade workflow that takes a device list and target versions, runs pre-checks, clears space, stages verified firmware, upgrades HA pairs in the right order inside an approved change window, verifies the result against a golden snapshot and ships an evidence pack, with no reboot ever executed without a human approval.

narration: hook

It is two in the morning. The change window is open, the firmware is uploaded, the H A pair is waiting, and the box says disk full. Again. The window closes, the ticket slips a week, and nobody slept.
hook

What if an agent had already cleared the space, staged the image with a verified checksum, run every pre-check, and asked you for one approval before the reboot? That is device upgrade automation, done with Claude, done safely.
intro
Gennoor Tech presents Device Upgrade Automation with Claude.
story

One device list in. One verified upgrade out, with evidence. You build the workflow in eleven modules, across F five, NetScaler, Radware and Cisco A C I. Claude plans, drafts and explains. Deterministic Python code executes. A person approves every space clear, install and reboot. And every call is logged.
path0

You start with how vendors actually upgrade: F five boot volumes and U C S archives, NetScaler build files, Alteon image banks, A C I firmware groups, and the ways upgrades fail in production. Then you set up Claude Code, the Claude Agent S D K and M C P servers that wrap the F five iControl REST A P I, the NetScaler NITRO A P I and the Radware Alteon A P I, read only to begin with, with strict J S O N outputs for every tool.
path0

Then discovery and pre-checks. You pull the inventory from the ServiceNow C M D B with the Table A P I, collect version, licence, H A role, sync state and disk usage from every device, and freeze a golden snapshot of virtual servers, pools, certificates and configuration backups. Claude reads the snapshot and explains anything that looks wrong before you touch a thing. No backup, no upgrade.
path1

Day two is the work itself. Deterministic adapters clear old images, core files and stale backups from allowlisted paths, dry-run first, to make room. They upload the firmware with S H A two five six verification and install it to the inactive boot volume. Upgrades run H A aware: standby first, verify, fail over, then the former active. The agent proposes the order and the exact A P I calls as structured J S O N. The code runs the approved plan and records state after every step. Nothing is improvised.
path2

Then verification. The post-check snapshot is diffed against the golden snapshot: version, virtual server status, pool members, H A sync, certificate expiry. Claude turns the diff into a structured verdict with a rollback recommendation, and the guardrail module enforces it. Allowlisted tools and devices, read only by default, a ServiceNow change request for every window, a human gate before every space clear, install and reboot, and an append-only audit log of every prompt, plan and call. You will try to talk the agent into skipping a check, and watch the runner refuse.
path3

Day three adds the scheduler. Approved change windows come from ServiceNow, runs are triggered through GitHub Actions, and the runner refuses to start outside the window. Reminders go out before, progress during, and a summary after. When a window is about to overrun, the run pauses at the next safe step and asks for an extension instead of leaving a device half upgraded.
path3

Then you scale to the fleet. Cisco A C I upgrades follow the process Cisco prescribes, with the pre-upgrade validator and A P I C firmware groups, controllers first, then switches in groups. Batches get canary devices, blast radius limits and stop on first failure, and the same adapter contract extends to other load balancers, Anaya L B included. The capstone runs a scheduled, approved, H A aware upgrade across a mixed fleet, end to end, and ships the evidence pack as a GitHub pull request.
labs

Every lab runs against simulated and lab devices with fictional hostnames. You will fill a disk on purpose, watch the pre-check gate stop an upgrade, fail a post-check deliberately, and roll back to the previous boot volume under time pressure.
stats
Eleven build modules. Three days, hands-on. Four vendor families. And zero reboots without approval.
